newsitem.title: FRANCE: French doctors say strike to go on, ease protests.
newsitem.headline: French doctors say strike to go on, ease protests.

text.p: Junior doctors pledged on Thursday to press on with three-week-old strike in French hospitals after talks with the government, but they promised to soften their protests about spending cuts given the state's readiness for dialogue.

The strike has become a test of conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe's resolve to cut welfare costs and reduce the state deficit to a level which will allow France to qualify for the European Union's planned single currency in 1999. The government has rejected the junior doctors' demands and accused them of promoting their own sectional interests.

A demonstration bringing together the striking junior doctors, other hospital staff unhappy about cuts in medical funding and the Communist-led CGT, one of France's biggest labour unions, was scheduled for Thursday afternoon in Paris.

After five hours of talks that lasted into early Thursday with Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot, the doctors' representatives called a halt to surprise protests which they have launched in various cities, including sit-ins outside the presidential palace in Paris and demonstrations delaying trains.

"But firmness and mobilisation are still on our agenda... This is no time for doctors to go back to work as their demands have not yet been met," a spokesman for the strikers said. Unions are due to meet Barrot and junior Health Minister Herve Gaymard again on Friday.
The stoppage, against spending curbs that would fine doctors in regions that overshoot state cash limits, has spread to 23 of France's 26 teaching hospitals.

Unions representing specialists in private practice, who have opposed the reforms from the time they were announced in late 1995 and who have allied themselves with the junior doctors, have called for a national demonstration on April 13.
